translation: Stick a finger through your throat.
about: The most famous Czech tongue twister. Four words and not one vowel letter: in each word the r carries the syllable, as a vowel would.
tips: Each word is one syllable, and the r is its core. Do not slip in a hidden vowel: krk, not kerk.
Stress the start of every word, so you get four even beats.
The z of skrz sounds like s, because the k after it is voiceless.

text: Smrž pln skvrn zvlhl z mlh.
translation: A morel full of spots grew damp from the mists.
about: A whole sentence with no vowel letters at all. Here l takes a turn as the core of the syllable as well as r.
tips: Zvlhl has two syllables, zvl-hl, each built round an l.
Word-final ž and h lose their voice: smrž ends in a sh sound, mlh in a ch sound.
Z and mlh are said as one word, with no pause between them.
steps: Smrž pln skvrn zvlhl z mlh.

about: A two-word warm-up. In vlky and plky the l works as the vowel of the first syllable.
tips: Hold the l for a moment, as you would a vowel: vl-ky, pl-ky.
The y at the end is a short i sound, as in bit.

translation: The chaplain wept in the chapel.
trains: p, k and l in quick succession
about: Short and gentle, but the same three consonants keep swapping places, which trips the tongue at speed.
tips: The v before kapli sounds like f and joins the next word: fkapli.
Czech p and k have no puff of air after them, unlike English p and k.

text: Šel pštros s pštrosicí a pštrosáčaty.
translation: An ostrich went walking with a female ostrich and their ostrich chicks.
about: A drill for š and č, with the pšt cluster four times over.
tips: Pšt is one quick movement: lips for p, then sh, then a light t.
The lone s joins the next word: spštrosicí.
Keep the long vowels long: pštrosicí, pštrosáčaty.
steps: Šel pštros s pštrosicí a pštrosáčaty.

text: Kmotře Petře, nepřepepřete mi toho vepře.
translation: Godfather Peter, don't over-pepper that pork for me.
ipa: kmotr̝̊ɛ pɛtr̝̊ɛ nɛpr̝̊ɛpɛpr̝̊ɛtɛ mɪ toɦo vɛpr̝̊ɛ
about: A rhyming drill with ř six times, always straight after p or t.
tips: After p and t, ř loses its voice and sounds more hissed than buzzed.
Nepřepepřete has five syllables: ne-pře-pe-pře-te. Say it slowly before you speed up.
steps: Kmotře Petře, nepřepepřete mi toho vepře.

translation: On the training ground, four marmots squeak.
about: A workout for the hissing and hushing sounds: s, š, c and č, side by side.
tips: Keep s and š apart: s with the tongue tip behind the teeth, š with the tongue drawn back and the lips rounded.
In cvičišti, svišti and piští, the ti is soft, like the t in tune in older British English.
Ř in čtyři sits between vowels, so it keeps its full buzz.

text: Tři sta třicet tři stříbrných stříkaček stříkalo přes tři sta třicet tři stříbrných střech.
translation: Three hundred and thirty-three silver fire hoses sprayed over three hundred and thirty-three silver roofs.
ipa: tr̝̊ɪ sta tr̝̊ɪt͡sɛt tr̝̊ɪ str̝̊iːbr̩niːx str̝̊iːkat͡ʃɛk str̝̊iːkalo pr̝̊ɛs tr̝̊ɪ sta tr̝̊ɪt͡sɛt tr̝̊ɪ str̝̊iːbr̩niːx str̝̊ɛx
about: The classic drill for ř, the sound most learners find hardest. Czechs use it to tease each other too.
tips: Here ř always follows t or p, so it is the voiceless, hissing kind.
Get stř right on its own first: s, then t, then ř, with no vowel between.
Stříbrných has a syllabic r in the middle: stří-br-ných.
steps: tři sta třicet tři stříbrných střech
stříkalo přes tři sta třicet tři stříbrných střech
Tři sta třicet tři stříbrných stříkaček stříkalo přes tři sta třicet tři stříbrných střech.

text: Nenaolejuje-li je Julie, naolejuji je já.
translation: If Julie doesn't oil them, I'll oil them myself.
ipa: nɛnaolɛjujɛlɪ jɛ julɪjɛ naolɛjujɪ jɛ jaː
about: No hard consonants at all, which is the trap: a long run of vowels, j and l where it is easy to lose count.
tips: Nenaolejuje-li is one word of seven syllables: ne-na-o-le-ju-je-li.
Keep the air flowing; there is no stop anywhere until the comma.
Julie is said in three syllables: Ju-li-je.
steps: Nenaolejuje-li je Julie, naolejuji je já.
